title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon tops an index rebuilt the day before
summary: Gemini 4 Carbon takes first place on Artificial Analysis's brand-new Intelligence Index v5, but only cyber defenders can use it so far, and the rebuilt index has its own trust problem. Plus Anthropic's Claude Enterprise reports that measure Claude's value from Claude's own transcripts, and what OpenAI's election war room actually watches.

topics: Gemini 4 Carbon (Google, 28 October 2026): 'our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities'; limited release to a subset of cyber defenders, expanding to trusted partners via the Fairwind Program, broader release 'coming soon' while iterating on guardrails; in the US government's voluntary pre-release testing; price $2/$10 per M tokens introductory (same as Argon), then $4/$20, cached input 95% off; SEC-bench Pro 88.2%, ExploitGym 54.8%, CWE-bench 71.0%, 'evaluated without guardrails'; Gray Swan indirect prompt injection 0.0% vs Argon 0.7% (attempt count and guardrail status not stated); Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 score 59, #1. Artificial Analysis v5 (announced 27 October): nine evals, four 25% buckets (knowledge work, coding, science, general incl. non-hallucination), shift to private benchmarks; Kimi K3.1 Pro went from 55 (3 behind the leader, old index, aired 25 October) to best open model behind eight closed models (Lambert's plot). Lambert: index 'signs of strain' (GPT-6.1 Terra above Fable 5.1), 'you can always shift the numbers to match your narrative', 'the benchmarking industry comes down to trust', AA revenue from labs it evaluates, wants more indices with different biases. Unresolved on air: Ada says defenders-first is a deliberate choice of who's first in line and frontier always looks like this from outside; Alan says a #1 on a private test for a model he can't call is two layers of 'trust us'.

Anthropic Claude Enterprise smart reports, in-app surveys, pooled group budgets (28 October 2026; help page still says beta): Claude analyzes a sample of a team's transcripts (up to 28 days; chat, Claude Code, Cowork) into workstreams with spend, deliverables, friction (missing connector, failed tool call); recommendations to build skills and repo rules; admins can raise spend limits from the report; attribution off by default, reveals logged; not for individual performance or employment decisions; restricted topics (health, union activity, political views, personal life) aggregate-only, can't be disabled; 10 free reports per org per month; not available with CMEK/HIPAA/hybrid. Surveys default question on what would break if access ended. Pooled budgets with member limits, alerts at 50/75/95/100%. TechCrunch/Jellyfish (276,000 customers): Anthropic-model tools ~a third of proposed code changes, spend up 10x since January, ~2% of engineering cost; Arcolano 'growth that most CFOs didn't plan for'; Albarran 'FDE-lite', 'that cost to switch is not zero'. On air: Ada's objection that the product grades itself and the survey is loaded; Alan's position that the friction list is the honest, usable part.

OpenAI Election Operations Center (Politico's Calder McHugh, 28 October 2026): led by Josh Lawson, head of civic and strategic risk; staffing in the hundreds; this week until votes counted after 3 November; watches abuse of OpenAI's own tools, unexpected model behavior reports, flagged accounts, Democracy Works and AP integrations; cartoonification of realistic nonexistent polling-place images; Meta has similar centers; Brennan Center (per Politico) found ChatGPT the only one of six tools with significant progress since May. OpenAI 8 October threat report (via Unite.AI): Russia's Dark Clark (Latin America, first Category 5, ChatGPT used mostly for internal reports to a superior) and Iran's Bogus Bylines (seven fake journalist personas, ~100 articles, ~a dozen outlets, Category 4). On air: Ada's objection that a war room catches accounts, not slow multi-turn drift (callback to the 22 October Transformer jailbreak), and open-weight models have no war room; Alan's test: a published post-election report on cases and response times.

dives.story: Gemini 4 Carbon and Artificial Analysis v5
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone choosing a frontier API (815 HN points) needs to know the new #1 is gated to cyber defenders and that the leaderboard they rank by was rebuilt on private tests the day before, so old scores no longer compare.

dives.story: Anthropic's Claude Enterprise smart reports and pooled budgets
dives.why_it_matters: Finance and platform teams facing agent bills that grew tenfold this year get a vendor-written ROI tool, and need to know which part is usable signal (friction) and which is the product grading itself.
Five days before the midterms, election officials and trust-and-safety teams need to know that the leading AI lab's war room watches its own product, not the wider ecosystem or open-weight models.

lore.note: Alan staked out that he'd turn on vendor-written AI value reports but read only the friction findings (missing connectors, failing tool calls), treating the vendor's value claims and loaded surveys as sales instruments.
